human_tolerance.notes: Highly urban and colonial: it builds huge communal stick nests on trees, pylons and buildings, and is described as very common in its native range. Bold around people.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Judgement. The article gives clutch size and incubation but no regional calendar window; a spring-to-early-summer window is used for the southern-hemisphere breeding season.

vocalizations.description: A loud, throaty 'chape(-yee)' or 'quak quak, quak-wi quarr', given in the colony's continuous loud calling from a perch or at the nest.
A penetrating 'skveet' screech, the harsh alarm note the colony gives when a bird is startled at the nest.

taxonomy.note: Rank and accepted name from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy.

external.note: GBIF usage key from the GBIF Backbone match for the scientific name; iNaturalist taxon id and Wikidata Q-id from Wikidata.

conservation.note: The article's taxobox gives the IUCN status as LC.

range.note: The article describes the species as native to South America and 'very common' there, with the Spanish article giving a Chilean extent from Arica to Puerto Montt, and documents introductions from the pet trade into North America, the Caribbean, Europe, the Middle East and Australasia. The native list is a conservative selection of the South American core range and introduced lists only the United States, the clearest documented case; neither list is an exhaustive transcription of the article's subsections.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: The bird hops and climbs through branches and around its nest structures and flies strongly and in flocks; the shared perching-songbird program forages by hop, so Hop is the declared ground gait. It also walks on the ground, which the chosen program does not represent. Swimming is not described.

traits.nest_type.note: The species' defining feature is a large enclosed stick nest with a central chamber that the pair builds and defends as a colony; the enclosed chamber is what the schema calls a cavity.

traits.perching.note: Parrots perch by definition; the bird is described perching and clambering on its nest and in trees.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits 1.0 BirdFuncDat row for Myiopsitta monachus: BodyMass-Value 120 g, the top of the stated range.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 'The nominate subspecies of this parrot is 29 cm long on average, with a 48 cm wingspan, and weighs 95-120 g.'

traits.length_m.note: 'The nominate subspecies of this parrot is 29 cm long on average'.

traits.wingspan_m.note: 'with a 48 cm wingspan' - recorded as 0.48 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Monk parakeets have an average lifespan in their natural environment of 6 years. However, monk parakeets in captivity can reach 25-30 years.' The wild average is used; the captivity figure is not a field lifespan.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Diet-Inv 10, Diet-Fruit 30, Diet-Seed 30, Diet-PlantO 30 (BirdFuncDat row, Diet-Certainty A); Diet-PlantO is mapped to the schema's fruit share, giving 0.6 fruit in total. The article is consistent: 'their diet mostly consists of seeds, fruits and vegetables, and grains', though it calls the bird primarily herbivorous.

traits.social.note: 'Monk parakeets also sometimes breed in groups, with a Barcelona-based study finding that about 20% of monk parakeet breeding units are composed of three to five birds.' The species nests colonially, so structure is Colony with the group sizes that study reports.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits 1.0 Nocturnal 0; the bird feeds and calls by day.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flushes from a feeding patch to a perch or back to its nest, the escape the shared perching-songbird program encodes.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from the described boldness of a colonial parrot that feeds in the open and nests on buildings and pylons in populated areas.

habitat.use.note: ForStrat-ground 20, ForStrat-understory 20, ForStrat-midhigh 40, ForStrat-canopy 20; the mid-high and canopy shares are mapped to arboreal, giving 0.2 ground against 0.8 arboreal.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Rests and breeds inside the enclosed chamber of its own nest structure, which is the clearest cavity user of any species in this locale.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow the EltonTraits diet shares; the cavity nesting weight of 1.0 reflects that the bird builds and defends its own enclosed nest, and the perch tag reflects its clambering and perching.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity and uses_gardens from the described colonial nesting on trees and structures in populated landscapes and from the species' ubiquity in towns; road_mortality and light_max are judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: The species is a permanent resident in its native range, breeding in every month of the year.

seasonal.phases.note: The article gives 'Their 1-11 white eggs are incubated continuously by the female' but no regional calendar window; the phase dates are a judgement for the southern-hemisphere spring and summer.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The article gives a 1-11 egg clutch and continuous female incubation but no day counts; duration_days 45 is a documented judgement for a parrot incubation and nestling period, not a sourced figure, and scale is a judgement for a recently fledged bird.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The call is a loud and throaty chape(-yee) or quak quaki quak-wi quarr.'

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'and screeches skveet' - the separate alarm screech described in the same sentence.

look.note: 'It has bright-green upperparts. The forehead and breast are pale grey with darker scalloping and the rest of the underparts are very light-green to yellow. The remiges are dark blue, and the tail is long and tapering. The bill is orange.' Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: seed-based foraging, an October-December nest-building window, and a long flee distance for a bold colonial parrot that is slow to alarm. The limitation to note in the pull request: this program is written for songbirds, so the parakeet's climbing is declared in traits but not animated.
